# Local security patch of braces 3.0.3

This is a repository-local derivative, `@confovhh/braces-depth-guard@3.0.3-confovhh.1`, of the MIT-licensed [braces 3.0.3](https://github.com/micromatch/braces/tree/3.0.3). It is not an upstream release. Original authorship, license, package metadata and documentation are retained in `LICENSE`, `UPSTREAM-package.json` and `UPSTREAM-README.md`; original package file hashes are in `UPSTREAM-SHA256.json`.

[GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) reports stack exhaustion from deeply nested input. The advisory lists no patched upstream version as of 2026-10-22. The patch rejects more than 100 nested structural blocks before recursive processing. The iterative parser guard covers braces, parentheses and mixtures. An iterative preflight also guards direct AST inputs to `compile`, `expand` and `stringify`, including child cycles. Malformed AST children that are not arrays and defined values that are not strings are rejected with `ERR_BRACES_INVALID_AST`, preventing alternative iterable or nested-array shapes from bypassing the guard. Normal `parent` and `prev` backlinks are ignored. The guard is fixed; an option cannot disable it. Rejected input throws a `SyntaxError` with code `ERR_BRACES_MAX_DEPTH`, rather than exhausting the call stack.

Changed upstream implementation files: `lib/parse.js`, `lib/compile.js`, `lib/expand.js` and `lib/stringify.js`. Added implementation: `lib/depth-guard.js`. The remaining upstream implementation bytes are unchanged. `package.json` gives this derivative a distinct name and version and removes unused upstream development tooling. The root manifest installs it under the compatibility name `braces` and uses `$braces` to redirect transitive consumers to the same local package.

This mitigates the specified nesting vulnerability. It does not claim to make arbitrary glob expressions safe against every possible resource-exhaustion pattern. ConfoVHH uses this package for developer tooling, not scientific input parsing. The public security advisory registry does not assess this local derivative; its security check is the committed `tests/braces-depth-guard.test.mjs`, alongside upstream compatibility checks and the full app gates. No advisory exception is added.

Revisit this local patch when an upstream fix becomes available. Remove the local override only after the replacement passes the depth-regression tests and the app release checks.
